info.title: MLXJev Swift abstractions for OneJev models

metadata.displayText: The https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift library provides MLX abstractions for MLX, MLXNN, MLXLM, MLXOptimizers and MLXRandom. But the new SystemOneModels from TypesafeAI Jev uses a new approach. I've found a python MLX jev port https://github.com/bnsd55/jevmlx#readme but Just like apple abstracted MLX into Swift native APIs I want to implement in this package a MLXJev target that ports the Jev system one models abstractions to swift. Our final goal will be to run https://github.com/OmniJev/OneJev models using MLX Swift. Plan it

messages.text: The https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift library provides MLX abstractions for MLX, MLXNN, MLXLM, MLXOptimizers and MLXRandom. But the new SystemOneModels from TypesafeAI Jev uses a new approach. I've found a python MLX jev port https://github.com/bnsd55/jevmlx#readme but Just like apple abstracted MLX into Swift native APIs I want to implement in this package a MLXJev target that ports the Jev system one models abstractions to swift. Our final goal will be to run https://github.com/OmniJev/OneJev models using MLX Swift. Plan it

content.text:
**Planning repository inspection**

I need to inspect the repo, but maybe it’s best to just plan the request for now rather than implementing changes. I’ll read through the codebase and any relevant upstream information I can find online. I’m not sure if my skills in Swift are up to par, and maybe SwiftUI isn’t even relevant here. I’ll explore the source structure and project using tools and the shell. First, I’ll provide a commentary update before checking local files and web URLs.

# jevmlx

[](#jevmlx)

[![CI](https://github.com/bnsd55/jevmlx/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bnsd55/jevmlx/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Build](https://github.com/bnsd55/jevmlx/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bnsd55/jevmlx/actions/workflows/build.yml) [![License: MIT](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/08cef40a9105b6526ca22088bc514fbfdbc9aac1ddbf8d4e6c750e3a88a44dca/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f4c6963656e73652d4d49542d626c75652e737667)](/bnsd55/jevmlx/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Python 3.12](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/b566d396d2e22b5a6a8b05f1168f96e80fb8e42d45d17cd178a039e81a2b047a/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f707974686f6e2d332e31322d626c75652e737667)](/bnsd55/jevmlx/blob/main/pyproject.toml)

jevmlx turns a schema of fields (booleans, enums, multi-selects) and a context string into a single batched forward pass on a local Apple Silicon model. Every allowed option for every field is scored from logits in one prefill — no text generation — and the JSON is assembled from the winners, with a probability per field.

## Quickstart

[](#quickstart)

```
git clone https://github.com/bnsd55/jevmlx && cd jevmlx && ./setup.sh
jevmlx decide --preset support_triage --json          # one decision, CLI
jevmlx serve --model fast --port 8000                  # HTTP server
curl -s localhost:8000/decide -d '{"schema":{"x":{"type":"enum","choices":["a","b"],"description":"d"}},"context":"pick one"}'
```

Requires an Apple Silicon Mac (M1+) and Python 3\.12+. First use of a model alias downloads weights (\~2 GB `fast`, \~4.5 GB `quality`).

## Why not structured output

[](#why-not-structured-output)

Structured output asks the model to write the JSON, token by token, then parses it and retries on failure. When the answer set is known and finite, that is the wrong tool. jevmlx reads one logits vector per field, applies a restricted softmax over the allowed options, and assembles the JSON itself — valid by construction, every field scored in one forward pass. When free text must be written (a summary, a rewrite), use generation; when the answer is one of N known choices, use scoring.

## Design your schema

[](#design-your-schema)

- **Options must be mutually exclusive.** A restricted softmax puts all probability mass on the listed options. If two can both be true, split into separate boolean fields or use a multi-select.

- **Add an escape option when the list may not be exhaustive.** A restricted softmax cannot say "none of these" unless you give it one. Add an `other` or `escalate` choice, or use `allow_none_of_above=True` (adds an explicit NONE\_OF\_ABOVE that maps to `None`; the field must be `Optional`).

- **Use `ordered=True` for scales.** An enum declared `ordered` (schema `"ordered": True`, or Pydantic `Field(json_schema_extra={"ordered": True})`) adds ordinal telemetry — `argmax_level`, `expected_index` (Σ pᵢ·i), `expected_score_normalized` — with no extra model call. Use it for severity, priority, or any monotonic scale.

- **Set review thresholds from labeled data.** `abstain_below_margin=X` withholds a field whose `probability_margin` (top1 − top2) falls below the cut. Fit the threshold on labeled examples — not by feel — so the abstention rate matches your review capacity. `probability_margin` and `threshold_distance` (multi) are on every `FieldResult`.

- **`labels` is the default scorer** (measured better on the 7B); `slots` scores single-token letter codes and is cheaper for very long option lists. Pass `scoring="slots"` to `decide`/`decide_many` or `--scoring slots` on the CLI to switch.

## Use it from Python

[](#use-it-from-python)

```
from typing import Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from jevmlx import decide


class Ticket(BaseModel):
    urgent: bool
    category: Literal["BILLING", "TECHNICAL", "FEEDBACK"] = Field(
        description="What the ticket is about",
        json_schema_extra={"choice_descriptions": {"BILLING": "invoices, charges, refunds"}},
    )
    tags: list[Literal["refund", "login", "performance"]] = []


result = decide(Ticket, "Customer was charged twice and wants the duplicate refunded.")
for name, f in result.fields.items():
    print(f"{name}: {f.value} (p={f.probability})")
```

`decide(...)` returns a `Decision`: `.value` (a validated `Ticket`), `.latency_ms`, `.fields` — one `FieldResult` per field with `value`, `probability`, `alternatives` (top 3), `probability_margin`, `legal_mass` (probability mass in allowed continuations — a leakage signal when low), `ordinal` (ordered enums only), and `semantics` (how the probability was produced). See [ARCHITECTURE.md](/bnsd55/jevmlx/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full `FieldResult` contract.

Options: `decide_many(model_cls, contexts)` for batches; `constraints=[...]` for constrained MAP (implies / excludes / requires\_parent); `calibration=<path>` for fitted multi-selection; `prior_correction=True` to subtract the neutral-context prior.

### One-question helpers

[](#one-question-helpers)

For a single-field decision you don't need a Pydantic model — `choose`, `judge`, and `rate` synthesize a one-field schema and return a `FieldResult` directly.

```
from jevmlx import choose, judge, rate

# enum: pick one of N (dict = name -> description)
f = choose(context, {"supported": "evidence supports", "contradicted": "evidence refutes"})
print(f.value, f.probability, f.probability_margin)

# boolean: yes/no (probability of True is f.probability)
f = judge(passage, "Is the claim supported by the passage?")

# ordinal: rate on a scale (declaration order = scale order)
f = rate(review, {"low": "poor", "medium": "ok", "high": "great"})
print(f.ordinal.argmax_level, f.ordinal.expected_score_normalized)
```

CLI mirrors: `jevmlx choose --context ctx.txt --option name=description ...`, `jevmlx judge --context ctx.txt --question "..."`, `jevmlx rate --context ctx.txt --level name=description ...`.

## Use it from any OpenAI-compatible server

[](#use-it-from-any-openai-compatible-server)

Instead of loading a model locally, jevmlx can send the same prompts to a chat server that returns logprobs (Ollama, vLLM, etc.):

```
jevmlx decide --backend openai --base-url http://localhost:11434/v1 --api-model llama3.2 --schema ticket.json --context ticket.txt
```

Tradeoff: one request per field (slower than one pass), and only the server's top-k logprobs are visible — options missing from that list get a floor probability and `truncated: true` in the telemetry.

## Serve over HTTP

[](#serve-over-http)

`jevmlx serve` loads a model once and serves decisions on a local port. One Metal GPU, one serial worker, a bounded admission queue in front.

```
jevmlx serve --model fast --port 8000
```

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/decide` | `{"schema": {...}, "context": "...", "temperature": 1.0}` \-\> per-field result dict |
| `POST` | `/v1/systemone` | `{"state": str\|object, "questions": {id: {type, instructions, criteria}}}` \-\> `{model, answers, usage}` (maps to one schema, same queue as /decide) |
| `GET` | `/v1/models` | `{"data": [{"id": <model id>, "owned_by": "jevmlx"}]}` |
| `GET` | `/health` | Process liveness (always 200). Carries `queue_depth`, `queue_capacity`, `worker_alive` |
| `GET` | `/ready` | `503` until model load \+ warm-up complete AND worker alive, then `200` |

Backpressure: **429 \+ `Retry-After`** when the queue is full (`--queue-size`, default 16); **413** when a request exceeds `--max-rows` (default 2048) or `--max-prompt-tokens` (default 8192), before any model work. The client's `X-Request-Id` is echoed; `queue_depth` and `queue_wait_ms` ride every response.

## How it works

[](#how-it-works)

The schema compiles per tokenizer: a codebook search picks the neutral alias codes whose candidate rows tokenize most cleanly, and the prompt renders from the compiled plan. The context is fenced with a per-context nonce so no interior line can impersonate the closing fence. The rendered prompt is a tested contract — [PROMPT\_PROTOCOL.md](/bnsd55/jevmlx/blob/main/PROMPT_PROTOCOL.md) documents it, and golden vectors (`benchmarks/golden_prompts.py --check`, run in CI) fail on any renderer drift.

The model prefills once and the KV cache is shared. One scoring row per field (extra trie rows for multi-token options), a restricted softmax over each field's allowed options, and the JSON is assembled from the winners. Chunks are sized by a measured active-memory budget; Metal allocation failures halve the chunk and retry. Temperature is applied once at the end; ties resolve deterministically. [ARCHITECTURE.md](/bnsd55/jevmlx/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md) has the full picture.

## Quick start

[](#quick-start)

Choose one backend, then run the Python example below.

### Option A: Flide

[](#option-a-flide)

For NVIDIA GPUs. Supports text, images and video. [Flide](https://github.com/OmniJev/Flide) is our inference engine for decision models.

```
uv venv -p 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install flide torchvision
flide serve --model OmniJev/OneJev1.6-0.8B --port 8000
```

### Option B: llama.cpp

[](#option-b-llamacpp)

For GGUF models. Supports text and images; use Flide for video. Install [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md) first (`brew install llama.cpp` on macOS).

```
pip install git+https://github.com/OmniJev/OneJev.git
qev serve --gguf mradermacher/OneJev1.6-0.8B-GGUF:Q8_0 --port 8000
```

### Option C: Docker

[](#option-c-docker)

The repo ships a Compose stack that detects your hardware and starts one backend. The llama.cpp profiles download `mradermacher/OneJev1.6-0.8B-GGUF:Q8_0` on first start; set `QEV_GGUF` in `docker/.env` for another size or quant.

```
cp docker/.env.example docker/.env   # set HF_TOKEN for gated/private repos
./docker/start.sh                    # auto-detect (Windows: .\docker\start.ps1)
./docker/start.sh logs               # follow logs
./docker/start.sh down               # stop every profile
```

Force a backend with `./docker/start.sh <torch|rocm|vulkan|gguf|gguf-rocm|cpu>` (add `--build` to rebuild). Every profile serves the API and the playground on :8000. On Windows only `torch` (NVIDIA) and `cpu` are available.

### Send a request

[](#send-a-request)

The server answers at `http://localhost:8000`. In another terminal, run this example with your own `screenshot.png`:

```
IMG=$(base64 -w0 screenshot.png)
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @- <<EOF
{
  "state": {"task": "Pay the open invoice from ACME", "screen": "<image:1>"},
  "media": [{"type": "image", "data": "data:image/png;base64,$IMG"}],
  "questions": {
    "done": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "The invoice has been paid"},
    "next": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What should the agent do next?",
             "criteria": {"click": "click an element", "type": "type text", "scroll": "scroll", "stop": "stop"}},
    "progress": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How far along is the task?",
                 "criteria": ["not started", "halfway", "almost done", "done"]}
  }
}
EOF
```

`answers.done.noul` is the probability of yes, `answers.next.probabilities` gives one probability per option and `answers.progress.score` is the expected level.

The API is compatible with TypeSafe System One. More examples: [video](/OmniJev/OneJev/blob/main/examples/video.py), [curl](/OmniJev/OneJev/blob/main/examples/curl.sh), [official TypeSafe SDK](/OmniJev/OneJev/blob/main/examples/official_sdk.py).

## Training

[](#training)

```
git clone https://github.com/OmniJev/OneJev.git
cd OneJev
pip install -e ".[train]"

# Choose A or B. A is enabled below.
# A. Demo: 100 examples with images (23 MB)
hf download OmniJev/OneJev-Data sample/sample-100.parquet --repo-type dataset --local-dir data/onejev
python -m train.unpack data/onejev --sample

# B. Full dataset: 94,707 examples (17.7 GB). Uncomment these two lines instead of A.
# hf download OmniJev/OneJev-Data --repo-type dataset --include "data/*.parquet" --local-dir data/onejev
# python -m train.unpack data/onejev
```

Either option creates `data/onejev/train.jsonl` and extracts images and video frames into `data/onejev/media/`.

[OneJev-Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OmniJev/OneJev-Data) releases 94,707 of the original 99,193 training questions; the remaining sources do not permit redistribution.

### Fine-tune

[](#fine-tune)

The four models fine-tune Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B for one epoch with the vision tower frozen. The configs use a learning rate of `5e-6`, a 16,384-token limit, and cross-entropy plus Brier loss over answer probabilities. To train the 4B model on four GPUs:

```
torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 -m train.sft --config train/configs/onejev_4b_full.yaml
```

Configs: [0\.8B](/OmniJev/OneJev/blob/main/train/configs/onejev_08b_full.yaml) · [4B](/OmniJev/OneJev/blob/main/train/configs/onejev_4b_full.yaml) · [9B](/OmniJev/OneJev/blob/main/train/configs/onejev_9b_full.yaml) · [27B](/OmniJev/OneJev/blob/main/train/configs/onejev_27b_full.yaml). Set `--nproc-per-node` to your GPU count; the 9B and 27B configs enable FSDP to shard model and optimizer state. For your own data, change `train` and `media_root` in the config.

The final 4B checkpoint is saved to `train/runs/onejev_4b/final`. Start it with:

```
flide serve --model train/runs/onejev_4b/final --format onejev --port 8000
```

# MLX Swift

[](#mlx-swift)

[**Installation**](#installation) \| [**Documentation**](https://swiftpackageindex.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift/main/documentation/mlx) \| [**Examples**](#examples)

MLX Swift is a Swift API for [MLX](https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/index.html).

MLX is an array framework for machine learning on Apple silicon. MLX Swift expands MLX to the Swift language, making research and experimentation easier on Apple silicon.

[View Current Release Planning](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Arelease-planning) and read about [Contributing](#contributing).

## Language Models

[](#language-models)

LLM and VLM implementations are available in [mlx-swift-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-lm).

## Examples

[](#examples)

MLX Swift has [many examples](https://swiftpackageindex.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift/main/documentation/mlx/examples), including:

- [MNISTTrainer](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-examples/blob/main/Applications/MNISTTrainer/README.md): An example that runs on both iOS and macOS that downloads MNIST training data and trains a [LeNet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeNet).

- [MLXChatExample](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-examples/blob/main/Applications/MLXChatExample/README.md): An example chat app that runs on both iOS and macOS that supports LLMs and VLMs.

- [LLMEval](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-examples/blob/main/Applications/LLMEval/README.md): A simple example that runs on both iOS and macOS that downloads an LLM and tokenizer from Hugging Face and generates text from a given prompt.

- [StableDiffusionExample](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-examples/blob/main/Applications/StableDiffusionExample/README.md): An example that runs on both iOS and macOS that downloads a stable diffusion model from Hugging Face and generates an image from a given prompt.

- [llm-tool](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-examples/blob/main/Tools/llm-tool/README.md): A command line tool for generating text using a variety of LLMs available on the Hugging Face hub.

The [MLX Swift Examples repo](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-examples) contains the complete code and documentation for these examples, including [guidelines on porting models](https://swiftpackageindex.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift-examples/main/documentation/mlxlmcommon/porting) from MLX Python.

## Installation

[](#installation)

The `MLX` Swift package can be built and run from Xcode or SwiftPM. A CMake installation is also provided, featuring a native Linux build option.

More details are in the [documentation](https://swiftpackageindex.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift/main/documentation/mlx/install).

### Xcode (1)

[](#xcode-1)

In Xcode you can add `https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift.git` as a package dependency and link `MLX`, `MLXNN`, `MLXOptimizers` and `MLXRandom` as needed.

### XCode (2)

[](#xcode-2)

Note that the SwiftPM and XCode (1) methods build `MLX` as a Library, not as a framework. It is possible to construct a situation where YourApp \-\> MLX, YourApp \-\> YourFramework and YourFramework \-\> MLX. This would give two copies of MLX in the resulting process and it may not work as expected.

If this cannot be avoided, either by making YourFramework a Library or having YourApp *not* link MLX, you can use the `xcode/MLX.xcodeproj` to build MLX as a *Framework*. This will require `mlx-swift` to be checked out adjacent or inside your project, possibly using git submodules, and dragging the `mlx-swift/xcode/MLX.xcodeproj` into your project. Once that is done your application can build and link MLX and related as Frameworks.

### SwiftPM

[](#swiftpm)

To use `MLX` with SwiftPM you can add this to your `Package.swift`:

```
dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift", from: "0.10.0")
]
```

and add the libraries as dependencies:

```
dependencies: [.product(name: "MLX", package: "mlx-swift"),
               .product(name: "MLXNN", package: "mlx-swift"),
               .product(name: "MLXOptimizers", package: "mlx-swift")]
```

Note

SwiftPM (command line) cannot build the Metal shaders so the ultimate build has to be done via Xcode.

### xcodebuild

[](#xcodebuild)

**Update the submodules**

The directories `Source/Cmlx/mlx` and `Source/Cmlx/mlx-c` are sourced as submodules. Before you attempt to build the project locally, pull down the updates for those submodules:

```
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

**Use Xcode to build the binaries and metal shaders**

Although `SwiftPM` (command line) cannot build the Metal shaders, `xcodebuild` can and it can be used to do command line builds:

```
# build and run tests
xcodebuild test -scheme mlx-swift-Package -destination 'platform=OS X'

# build Tutorial
xcodebuild build -scheme Tutorial -destination 'platform=OS X'
```

### CMake

[](#cmake)

#### (1) macOS

[](#1-macos)

**Install Dependencies**

Building with CMake requires both CMake and Ninja to be installed. You can do this with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/):

```
brew install cmake
brew install ninja
```

**Build \+ Run Examples**

- The examples use the Metal GPU backend by default on macOS.

- Note that the CUDA GPU backend is exclusive to Linux.

```
mkdir -p build
cd build
cmake .. -G Ninja
ninja
./example1
./tutorial
```

#### (2) Linux

[](#2-linux)

**Install Dependencies**

- To build the example binaries, install all dependencies listed in the CI [scripts](/ml-explore/mlx-swift/blob/main/.github/scripts).

- Note: The CUDA GPU backend requires the CUDA toolkit and additional dependencies.

- For Swift installation on Linux, visit [swift.org](https://www.swift.org/install/linux/).

**Build \+ Run Examples (CPU backend)**

On Linux, the examples use the CPU backend by default.

```
mkdir -p build
pushd build
cmake -DMLX_BUILD_METAL=OFF .. -G Ninja
ninja
./example1
./tutorial
popd
```

**Build \+ Run Examples (GPU CUDA backend)**

```
mkdir -p build
pushd build
cmake -DMLX_BUILD_METAL=OFF -DMLX_BUILD_CUDA=ON -DMLX_C_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF .. -G Ninja
ninja
./example1 --device gpu
./tutorial --device gpu
popd
```

## Contributing

[](#contributing)

Check out the [contribution guidelines](/ml-explore/mlx-swift/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information on contributing to MLX. See the [docs](https://swiftpackageindex.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift/main/documentation/mlx/install) for more information on building from source, and running tests.

We are grateful for all of [our contributors](/ml-explore/mlx-swift/blob/main/ACKNOWLEDGMENTS.md#Individual-Contributors). If you contribute to MLX Swift and wish to be acknowledged, please add your name to the list in your pull request.

Smaller, focused PRs are easier and quicker to review. Sometimes larger PRs can't be helped. If you want to discuss, feel free to open an issue or ask questions in a PR.

MLX Swift was initially developed by David Koski and Ronan Collobert, and is now maintained by David Koski. MLX Swift is built on top of [MLX](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx), which was initially developed with equal contribution by Awni Hannun, Jagrit Digani, Angelos Katharopoulos, and Ronan Collobert.

[](#versions)

All capabilities in MLX (Python) should be available in MLX Swift. If you encounter any that are missing please file an issue or feel free to submit a PR.

1: # MLXKit
2: 
3: A high-level Swift framework for machine learning on Apple silicon, built on [MLX Swift](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift).
4: 
5: MLXKit provides a typed training workflow: define a model, create a typed training configuration, and call `fit()`. It coordinates gradient computation, metric tracking, callbacks, learning-rate scheduling, and checkpointing while MLX and MLXOptimizers provide the numerical core.
6: 
7: ## Requirements
8: 
9: - macOS 27.x
10: - Swift 6.4 with Xcode 27.0
11: - Apple Silicon (`arm64`, M1 or later)
12: 
13: ## Installation
14: 
15: Add MLXKit to your `Package.swift`:
16: 
17: ```swift
18: dependencies: [
19:     .package(url: "https://github.com/murilxaraujo/MLXKit", from: "1.0.0"),
20: ]
21: ```
22: 
23: Then add it to your target:
24: 
25: ```swift
26: .target(name: "MyApp", dependencies: ["MLXKit"])
27: ```
28: 
29: ## Quick Start
30: 
31: ```swift
32: import MLX
33: import MLXNN
34: import MLXOptimizers
35: import MLXKit
36: 
37: // 1. Define a model
38: final class Classifier: Module, TrainableModel {
39:     let linear1 = Linear(inputDimensions: 784, outputDimensions: 128)
40:     let linear2 = Linear(inputDimensions: 128, outputDimensions: 10)
41: 
42:     func callAsFunction(_ input: MLXArray) -> MLXArray {
43:         var x = linear1(input)
44:         x = maximum(x, 0)
45:         return linear2(x)
46:     }
47: }
48: 
49: // 2. Configure
50: let model = Classifier()
51: let engine = TrainingEngine()
52: let config = TrainingConfiguration(
53:     optimizer: Adam(learningRate: 1e-3),
54:     objective: CrossEntropyLoss(),
55:     metrics: [Accuracy()],
56:     learningRateSchedule: CosineDecay(initialLR: 1e-3, totalSteps: 10000)
57: )
58: 
59: // 3. Train
60: let loader = try DataLoader(
61:     source: trainData,
62:     batchSize: 32,
63:     shuffle: .full(seed: 42)
64: )
65: let history = try await engine.fit(
66:     model, configuration: config, data: loader,
67:     epochs: 10,
68:     validationData: valLoader,
69:     callbacks: [ProgressReporter(), EarlyStopping(monitor: "val_loss", patience: 3)]
70: )
71: 
72: // 4. Evaluate & predict
73: let metrics = try await engine.evaluate(model, configuration: config, data: testLoader)
74: let output = engine.predict(model, input: newData)
75: 
76: // 5. Save & load
77: try Checkpointing.saveWeights(model, to: weightsURL)
78: try Checkpointing.loadWeights(into: restoredModel, from: weightsURL)
79: ```
80: 
81: ## Features
82: 
83: | Module | Description |
84: |---|---|
85: | **Training Engine** | Typed `fit()` / `evaluate()` / `predict()` over async batch sequences |
86: | **M5 Training Controls** | Ordered gradient transforms, global-norm clipping, sample-aware accumulation, and explicit sample/class-weighted cross entropy |
87: | **Losses** | CrossEntropy, BCE, MSE, L1, Huber, KLDiv with configurable reduction |
88: | **Metrics** | Accuracy, TopK, MSE, and MAE with batch accumulation; `RunningLoss` is a standalone helper |
89: | **Callbacks** | EarlyStopping, ModelCheckpoint, ProgressReporter, Lambda |
90: | **Data** | Typed indexed/async sample sources, composable transforms, seeded shuffle, batching, and bounded prefetch |
91: | **LR Schedules** | CosineDecay, StepDecay, ExponentialDecay, composable Warmup |
92: | **Serialization** | Versioned weight and inference artifacts; epoch-boundary recovery when an optimizer implements `CheckpointableOptimizer` |
93: | **Utilities** | `model.printSummary()` with tabular param counts and memory estimates |

1: # Architecture
2: 
3: MLXKit is a small coordination layer over MLX Swift and MLXOptimizers. It
4: provides typed model I/O, scalar objectives, metric aggregation, callbacks,
5: learning-rate schedules, and checkpoint helpers. MLX remains responsible for
6: tensor operations, autodiff, model parameters, and device execution.
7: 
8: ## Training flow
9: 
10: 1. Define a ``TrainableModel`` by declaring `Input` and `Output` and
11:    implementing `callAsFunction(_:)`.
12: 2. Create a ``TrainingConfiguration`` with an MLXOptimizers optimizer, an
13:    objective, optional typed metrics, and an optional learning-rate schedule.
14: 3. Call ``TrainingEngine/fit(_:configuration:data:epochs:resumeFrom:trainingStep:callbacks:)``
15:    with an asynchronous sequence of typed ``Batch`` values. The engine
16:    computes MLX gradients and applies one optimizer update per valid batch.
17: 4. Optionally provide a validation sequence. The engine logs `val_loss` and
18:    prefixes validation metrics with `val_` after each epoch.
19: 5. Call ``TrainingEngine/evaluate(_:configuration:data:trainingStep:)`` for
20:    inference-mode loss and metrics, or ``TrainingEngine/predict(_:input:)``
21:    for typed inference.
22: 
23: ## Component contracts
24: 
25: | Component | Responsibility |
26: |---|---|
27: | ``TrainableModel`` | Typed model input and complete output, backed by an MLX `Module`. |
28: | ``Objective`` / ``LossFunction`` | Compute a scalar differentiable objective. |
29: | ``Metric`` | Accumulate a named value across batches and reset at run boundaries. |
30: | ``Callback`` | Observe training lifecycle synchronously; callback errors propagate. |
31: | ``LRSchedule`` | Map successful optimizer-update steps to learning rates. |
32: | ``Dataset`` / ``DataLoader`` | Existing array-backed sample batching for MLX arrays. |
33: | ``Checkpointing`` | Persist and restore MLX model weights. |
34: 
35: ## M2 sequence boundary and M4 data pipeline
36: 
37: M2 training accepts an `AsyncSequence` whose elements are already typed
38: ``Batch`` values. M4's typed ``DataLoader`` builds those batches from indexed or
39: asynchronous sample sources, with transforms, seeded shuffle, collation, and
40: optional bounded prefetch. See <doc:DataPipeline> for examples and the source,
41: ordering, error, and cancellation contracts.
42: 
43: For scalar reduction, epoch aggregation, metric timing, schedules, lifecycle,
44: failure behavior, and model-mode restoration, see <doc:M2TrainingSemantics>.

1: # Compatibility and Release Policy
2: 
3: ## Before 2.0.0
4: 
5: MLXKit is in active pre-2.0 development. Source-breaking API changes are allowed
6: in any pre-2.0 release, including 1.x releases. Do not interpret a 1.x version
7: number as a promise that source code will compile unchanged with every later
8: pre-2.0 release. Release notes must identify breaking changes and give a
9: migration note when a change affects users.
10: 
11: The version number still communicates release scale, but pre-2.0 source
12: compatibility takes priority over preserving an API that blocks the 2.0 product
13: contract. Patch releases should normally contain fixes; if a breaking change is
14: necessary in a pre-2.0 patch, it must be called out explicitly rather than
15: hidden behind the patch number.
16: 
17: ## Starting with 2.0.0
18: 
19: The public source API is stable within a 2.x major version:
20: 
21: - Patch releases contain compatible fixes.
22: - Minor releases add functionality without removing or changing existing
23:   documented behavior incompatibly. Deprecations must include a replacement or
24:   clear migration advice.
25: - A source-breaking change requires a new major version and release notes with
26:   migration guidance.
27: 
28: This is a source-package compatibility policy. MLXKit does not promise binary
29: framework or ABI compatibility. Applications must rebuild against the Swift,
30: Xcode, operating-system, and MLX Swift versions listed as supported in
31: <doc:PlatformSupport>.
32: 
33: ## 1.x to 2.0 migration
34: 
35: The 2.0 release must include a migration guide with before-and-after examples
36: for changed model, data, training, callback, and persistence workflows. The
37: guide must call out removed APIs, changed semantics, and any required changes to
38: custom model or training code. Compatibility shims are not promised; the guide
39: must identify any shims that are actually provided rather than imply they
40: exist.
41: 
42: ## Limits of compatibility promises
43: 
44: - Pre-2.0 releases have no source-compatibility guarantee across releases.
45: - MLXKit cannot promise compatibility with MLX Swift versions outside the
46:   validated platform matrix or override upstream MLX API and behavior changes.
47: - No binary/ABI stability is promised.
48: - Cross-version compatibility is limited to the artifact versions and legacy
49:   readers explicitly documented in <doc:M6PersistenceSemantics>. Weight files,
50:   inference artifacts, progress metadata, and optimizer-aware training
51:   checkpoints are distinct and must not be assumed interchangeable.
52: - The supported platform/toolchain matrix is the limit of tested claims; a
53:   package manifest's version range does not itself establish validation.

1: # Platform and Backend Support
2: 
3: This matrix describes the MLXKit 2.0 support contract using the repository's
4: manifest, lockfile, CI workflow, and local validation. A package declaration or
5: successful compile alone is not proof that a configuration is supported.
6: 
7: ## Supported baseline
8: 
9: | Dimension | Supported baseline | Evidence and limits |
10: |---|---|---|
11: | Operating system | macOS 27.x on Apple silicon | `Package.swift` declares macOS 27 as the deployment minimum. The current local validation host is macOS 27.0.1. CI selects Xcode 27.0 and now requires and records macOS 27.x. Later macOS major versions are not yet separately validated. |
12: | Architecture | Apple silicon (`arm64`) | The package requirements and MLX GPU test path target Apple silicon. CI records `uname -m`; a run is evidence for arm64 only if its log reports `arm64`. |
13: | Swift and Xcode | Swift 6.4 with Xcode 27.0 | `swift-tools-version` is 6.4, the local validation host uses Swift 6.4 / Xcode 27.0, and CI selects Xcode 27.0. Other compiler versions are not a tested compatibility promise. |
14: | MLX Swift | 0.32.3 for the validated dependency resolution | `Package.swift` requires `mlx-swift` from 0.32.3 and `Package.resolved` pins 0.32.3. Other versions permitted by the package's version range are not covered by this validation. |
15: | Backend | Metal on Apple silicon for GPU-dependent execution | CI runs GPU-dependent tests through Xcode with `MLX_GPU_TESTS`. The ordinary `swift test` path runs non-GPU-dependent tests; it is not evidence for a separate CPU compute backend. |
16: 
17: The CI workflow performs a library build, the non-GPU-dependent test suite,
18: example smoke runs, and both library and example GPU-dependent test suites on
19: its `xcode-27` runner. Its environment-reporting
20: step records the OS, architecture, Xcode, Swift, and resolved MLX Swift version.
21: Treat a CI run as validation of the exact environment printed in its log, not
22: of every environment covered by a broad version range.
23: 
24: ## Experimental or unsupported configurations
25: 
26: - macOS 28 or later, newer Swift/Xcode versions, or MLX Swift versions other
27:   than the pinned 0.32.3 baseline are **experimental** until CI validates them.
28: - Intel Macs are **unsupported**; the published product requirement is Apple
29:   silicon and there is no Intel CI target.
30: - Linux, Windows, and non-Apple backends are **unsupported**; MLXKit has no
31:   package or CI target for them.
32: - A machine without Metal may run the non-GPU-dependent tests where its Swift
33:   toolchain can build the package, but it is not a supported MLXKit compute
34:   configuration.
35: 
36: ## Validation commands
37: 
38: The CI workflow runs these checks on the supported baseline:
39: 
40: ```bash
41: swift build
42: swift test
43: xcodebuild test \
44:   -scheme MLXKit \
45:   -destination 'platform=macOS' \
46:   -only-testing:MLXKitTests \
47:   OTHER_SWIFT_FLAGS='-DMLX_GPU_TESTS' \
48:   -parallel-testing-enabled NO
49: make smoke-examples
50: make test-examples-gpu
51: ```
52: 
53: Run `make test-all` locally to include the GPU-dependent suites. GPU validation
54: requires Apple silicon and Metal; example validation also requires Tuist. A change to the declared support baseline
55: must update this matrix and add or revise an executable CI validation path.

66: /// MLXKit does not serialize model code, model construction, tokenizers, or
67: /// inference caches. Training checkpoints additionally contain optimizer state
68: /// and epoch/update progress, when the optimizer conforms to
69: /// ``CheckpointableOptimizer``.
70: public enum Checkpointing {
71: 
72:     private static let formatName = "mlxkit.artifact"
73:     private static let formatVersion = "1"
74:     private static let formatKey = "mlxkit.format"
75:     private static let versionKey = "mlxkit.version"
76:     private static let kindKey = "mlxkit.kind"
77:     private static let modelPrefix = "model."
78:     private static let optimizerPrefix = "optimizer."
79: 
80:     /// Information stored in an inference artifact.
81:     public struct InferenceArtifactInfo: Sendable {
82:         /// Caller-provided metadata. This does not include executable model or
83:         /// tokenizer state.
84:         public let metadata: [String: String]
85:     }
86: 
87:     /// Information restored from an epoch-boundary training checkpoint.
88:     public struct TrainingCheckpointInfo: Sendable {
89:         public let progress: TrainingProgress
90:         public let metadata: [String: String]
91:         public let optimizerIdentifier: String
92:     }
93: 
94:     /// Information stored by the legacy model-plus-progress API.
95:     ///
96:     /// This is not a resumable training checkpoint: it contains model
97:     /// parameters and counters only, not optimizer state.
98:     @available(*, deprecated, message: "Use TrainingProgress and saveTrainingCheckpoint when optimizer recovery is required")
99:     public struct CheckpointInfo: Sendable {
100:         public let epoch: Int
101:         public let step: Int
102:         public let metadata: [String: String]
103:     }
104: 
105:     // MARK: Weights
106: 
107:     /// Saves a model's trainable parameters only.
108:     public static func saveWeights(_ model: Module, to url: URL) throws {
109:         try saveArtifact(
110:             arrays: prefixed(modelArrays(model), with: modelPrefix),
111:             metadata: [kindKey: "weights"],
112:             to: url
113:         )
114:     }
115: 
116:     /// Loads model trainable parameters from a weights, inference, or training
117:     /// artifact. The model is unchanged if artifact validation fails.
118:     @discardableResult
119:     public static func loadWeights(into model: Module, from url: URL) throws -> Module {
120:         let artifact = try readArtifact(from: url)
121:         guard artifact.kind == nil || ["weights", "inference", "training", "progress", "legacy-progress"].contains(artifact.kind!) else {
122:             throw CheckpointError.incompatibleArtifact(expected: "model weights", actual: artifact.kind!)
123:         }
124:         let parameters = try modelParameters(from: artifact.modelArrays, for: model, at: url)
125:         _ = model.update(parameters: parameters)
126:         return model
127:     }
128: 
129:     // MARK: Inference artifact
130: 
131:     /// Saves trainable parameters and caller-supplied inference metadata.
132:     ///
133:     /// This format does not serialize model construction, executable code,
134:     /// tokenizer files, or inference caches. Applications own those assets.
135:     public static func saveInferenceArtifact(
136:         _ model: Module,
137:         metadata: [String: String] = [:],
138:         to url: URL
139:     ) throws {
140:         try validateUserMetadata(metadata)
141:         var artifactMetadata = metadata
142:         artifactMetadata[kindKey] = "inference"
143:         try saveArtifact(
144:             arrays: prefixed(modelArrays(model), with: modelPrefix),
145:             metadata: artifactMetadata,
146:             to: url
147:         )
148:     }
149: 
150:     /// Loads an inference artifact's parameters and returns its caller metadata.
151:     /// Model parameters are not changed if validation fails.
152:     @discardableResult
153:     public static func loadInferenceArtifact(
154:         into model: Module,
155:         from url: URL
156:     ) throws -> InferenceArtifactInfo {
157:         let artifact = try readArtifact(from: url)
158:         guard artifact.kind == "inference" else {
159:             throw CheckpointError.incompatibleArtifact(
160:                 expected: "inference artifact", actual: artifact.kind ?? "legacy untyped weights"
161:             )
162:         }
163:         let parameters = try modelParameters(from: artifact.modelArrays, for: model, at: url)
164:         _ = model.update(parameters: parameters)
165:         return InferenceArtifactInfo(metadata: artifact.publicMetadata)
166:     }

168:     // MARK: Resumable training checkpoint
169: 
170:     /// Saves model parameters, optimizer state, and epoch-boundary progress.
171:     ///
172:     /// The caller must use the same model/objective/optimizer configuration and
173:     /// learning-rate schedule when resuming, and recreate the data sequence at
174:     /// the next epoch. Optimizer hyperparameters and custom state should be
175:     /// validated by the optimizer's `restoreCheckpointState(_:)` implementation.
176:     public static func saveTrainingCheckpoint(
177:         model: Module,
178:         optimizer: any CheckpointableOptimizer,
179:         progress: TrainingProgress,
180:         metadata: [String: String] = [:],
181:         to url: URL
182:     ) throws {
183:         try validate(progress: progress)
184:         try validateUserMetadata(metadata)
185:         guard !optimizer.checkpointIdentifier.isEmpty else {
186:             throw CheckpointError.invalidOptimizerIdentifier
187:         }
188: 
189:         let optimizerState = try optimizer.makeCheckpointState()
190:         var arrays = prefixed(modelArrays(model), with: modelPrefix)
191:         let optimizerArrays = prefixed(optimizerState.arrays, with: optimizerPrefix)
192:         for (key, value) in optimizerArrays {
193:             guard arrays.updateValue(value, forKey: key) == nil else {
194:                 throw CheckpointError.duplicateArrayKey(key)
195:             }
196:         }
197: 
198:         var artifactMetadata = metadata
199:         artifactMetadata[kindKey] = "training"
200:         artifactMetadata["mlxkit.completedEpochs"] = String(progress.completedEpochs)
201:         artifactMetadata["mlxkit.optimizerStep"] = String(progress.optimizerStep)
202:         artifactMetadata["mlxkit.optimizerIdentifier"] = optimizer.checkpointIdentifier
203:         for (key, value) in optimizerState.metadata {
204:             let prefixedKey = "mlxkit.optimizer.\(key)"
205:             guard artifactMetadata[prefixedKey] == nil else {
206:                 throw CheckpointError.reservedMetadataKey(prefixedKey)
207:             }
208:             artifactMetadata[prefixedKey] = value
209:         }
210:         try saveArtifact(arrays: arrays, metadata: artifactMetadata, to: url)
211:     }
212: 
213:     /// Saves a training checkpoint or throws when the optimizer does not
214:     /// implement the checkpoint-state capability.
215:     public static func saveTrainingCheckpoint(
216:         model: Module,
217:         optimizer: any Optimizer,
218:         progress: TrainingProgress,
219:         metadata: [String: String] = [:],
220:         to url: URL
221:     ) throws {
222:         guard let checkpointable = optimizer as? any CheckpointableOptimizer else {
223:             throw CheckpointError.unsupportedOptimizerRecovery(
224:                 String(reflecting: type(of: optimizer))
225:             )
226:         }
227:         try saveTrainingCheckpoint(
228:             model: model,
229:             optimizer: checkpointable,
230:             progress: progress,
231:             metadata: metadata,
232:             to: url
233:         )
234:     }
235: 
236:     /// Restores a training checkpoint into a model and a checkpoint-capable
237:     /// optimizer. The optimizer identifier is checked before either is changed.
238:     @discardableResult
239:     public static func loadTrainingCheckpoint(
240:         into model: Module,
241:         optimizer: any CheckpointableOptimizer,
242:         from url: URL
243:     ) throws -> TrainingCheckpointInfo {
244:         let artifact = try readArtifact(from: url)
245:         guard artifact.kind == "training" else {
246:             throw CheckpointError.incompatibleArtifact(
247:                 expected: "resumable training checkpoint", actual: artifact.kind ?? "legacy artifact"
248:             )
249:         }
250: 
251:         let expectedIdentifier = artifact.rawMetadata["mlxkit.optimizerIdentifier"] ?? ""
252:         guard expectedIdentifier == optimizer.checkpointIdentifier else {
253:             throw CheckpointError.optimizerMismatch(
254:                 expected: expectedIdentifier, actual: optimizer.checkpointIdentifier
255:             )
256:         }
257: 
258:         let progress = TrainingProgress(
259:             completedEpochs: try integerMetadata("mlxkit.completedEpochs", in: artifact.rawMetadata),
260:             optimizerStep: try integerMetadata("mlxkit.optimizerStep", in: artifact.rawMetadata)
261:         )
262:         try validate(progress: progress)
263:         let modelState = try modelParameters(from: artifact.modelArrays, for: model, at: url)
264:         let optimizerState = OptimizerCheckpointState(
265:             arrays: artifact.optimizerArrays,
266:             metadata: artifact.rawMetadata.reduce(into: [:]) { result, entry in
267:                 let prefix = "mlxkit.optimizer."
268:                 if entry.key.hasPrefix(prefix) {
269:                     result[String(entry.key.dropFirst(prefix.count))] = entry.value
270:                 }
271:             }
272:         )
273: 
274:         // The optimizer contract requires validation-before-mutation. The model
275:         // update is performed only after that potentially throwing operation.
276:         try optimizer.restoreCheckpointState(optimizerState)
277:         _ = model.update(parameters: modelState)
278:         return TrainingCheckpointInfo(
279:             progress: progress,
280:             metadata: artifact.publicMetadata,
281:             optimizerIdentifier: expectedIdentifier
282:         )
283:     }
284: 
285:     /// Restores a training checkpoint or throws when the optimizer does not
286:     /// implement the checkpoint-state capability.
287:     @discardableResult
288:     public static func loadTrainingCheckpoint(
289:         into model: Module,
290:         optimizer: any Optimizer,
291:         from url: URL
292:     ) throws -> TrainingCheckpointInfo {
293:         guard let checkpointable = optimizer as? any CheckpointableOptimizer else {
294:             throw CheckpointError.unsupportedOptimizerRecovery(
295:                 String(reflecting: type(of: optimizer))
296:             )
297:         }
298:         return try loadTrainingCheckpoint(
299:             into: model,
300:             optimizer: checkpointable,
301:             from: url
302:         )
303:     }

306: 
307:     /// Saves model parameters with progress metadata only.
308:     ///
309:     /// This is useful for reporting or application-managed epoch restarts. It
310:     /// does not save optimizer state and is not sufficient for faithful training
311:     /// recovery.
312:     public static func saveTrainingProgress(
313:         model: Module,
314:         progress: TrainingProgress,
315:         metadata: [String: String] = [:],
316:         to url: URL
317:     ) throws {
318:         try validate(progress: progress)
319:         try validateUserMetadata(metadata)
320:         var artifactMetadata = metadata
321:         artifactMetadata[kindKey] = "progress"
322:         artifactMetadata["mlxkit.completedEpochs"] = String(progress.completedEpochs)
323:         artifactMetadata["mlxkit.optimizerStep"] = String(progress.optimizerStep)
324:         try saveArtifact(arrays: prefixed(modelArrays(model), with: modelPrefix), metadata: artifactMetadata, to: url)
325:     }

327:     /// Loads model parameters and progress metadata without restoring an
328:     /// optimizer. This does not resume training with optimizer-equivalent state.
329:     @discardableResult
330:     public static func loadTrainingProgress(
331:         into model: Module,
332:         from url: URL
333:     ) throws -> (progress: TrainingProgress, metadata: [String: String]) {
334:         let artifact = try readArtifact(from: url)
335:         guard artifact.kind == "progress" || artifact.kind == "legacy-progress" else {
336:             throw CheckpointError.incompatibleArtifact(
337:                 expected: "training progress artifact", actual: artifact.kind ?? "legacy artifact"
338:             )
339:         }
340:         let progress: TrainingProgress
341:         if artifact.kind == "legacy-progress" {
342:             progress = TrainingProgress(
343:                 completedEpochs: Int(artifact.rawMetadata["mlxkit.epoch"] ?? "0") ?? 0,
344:                 optimizerStep: Int(artifact.rawMetadata["mlxkit.step"] ?? "0") ?? 0
345:             )
346:         } else {
347:             progress = TrainingProgress(
348:                 completedEpochs: try integerMetadata("mlxkit.completedEpochs", in: artifact.rawMetadata),
349:                 optimizerStep: try integerMetadata("mlxkit.optimizerStep", in: artifact.rawMetadata)
350:             )
351:         }
352:         try validate(progress: progress)
353:         let parameters = try modelParameters(from: artifact.modelArrays, for: model, at: url)
354:         _ = model.update(parameters: parameters)
355:         return (progress, artifact.publicMetadata)
356:     }

359:     /// state; use `saveTrainingCheckpoint` for recovery.

361:     public static func save(
362:         model: Module,
363:         epoch: Int,
364:         step: Int = 0,

369:             model: model,

371:             metadata: additionalMetadata,
372:             to: url

377:     /// state was restored.
378:     @available(*, deprecated, message: "This restores weights and progress metadata only; use loadTrainingCheckpoint for optimizer recovery")
379:     @discardableResult
380:     public static func load(into model: Module, from url: URL) throws -> CheckpointInfo {
381:         let restored = try loadTrainingProgress(into: model, from: url)
382:         return CheckpointInfo(
383:             epoch: restored.progress.completedEpochs,
384:             step: restored.progress.optimizerStep,

386:         )
387:     }

389:     // MARK: Validation and serialization helpers
390: 
391:     private struct Artifact {
392:         let kind: String?
393:         let modelArrays: [String: MLXArray]
394:         let optimizerArrays: [String: MLXArray]
395:         let rawMetadata: [String: String]
396:         let publicMetadata: [String: String]
397:     }
398: 
399:     private static func validate(progress: TrainingProgress) throws {
400:         guard progress.completedEpochs >= 0, progress.optimizerStep >= 0 else {
401:             throw CheckpointError.invalidProgress(
402:                 completedEpochs: progress.completedEpochs,
403:                 optimizerStep: progress.optimizerStep
404:             )
405:         }
406:     }
407: 
408:     private static func validateUserMetadata(_ metadata: [String: String]) throws {
409:         if let key = metadata.keys.first(where: { $0.hasPrefix("mlxkit.") }) {
410:             throw CheckpointError.reservedMetadataKey(key)
411:         }
412:     }
413: 
414:     private static func modelArrays(_ model: Module) -> [String: MLXArray] {
415:         Dictionary(model.trainableParameters().flattened(), uniquingKeysWith: { _, newer in newer })
416:     }
417: 
418:     private static func prefixed(
419:         _ arrays: [String: MLXArray],
420:         with prefix: String
421:     ) -> [String: MLXArray] {
422:         Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: arrays.map { (prefix + $0.key, $0.value) })
423:     }
424: 
425:     private static func saveArtifact(
426:         arrays: [String: MLXArray],
427:         metadata: [String: String],
428:         to url: URL
429:     ) throws {
430:         guard url.isFileURL else { throw CheckpointError.nonFileURL(url) }
431:         var completeMetadata = metadata
432:         completeMetadata[formatKey] = formatName
433:         completeMetadata[versionKey] = formatVersion
434: 
435:         let manager = FileManager.default
436:         let directory = url.deletingLastPathComponent()
437:         let temporaryURL = directory.appendingPathComponent(
438:             ".\(url.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent).\(UUID().uuidString).safetensors"
439:         )
440:         defer { try? manager.removeItem(at: temporaryURL) }
441: 
442:         do {
443:             try manager.createDirectory(at: directory, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
444:             try MLX.save(arrays: arrays, metadata: completeMetadata, url: temporaryURL)
445:             if manager.fileExists(atPath: url.path(percentEncoded: false)) {
446:                 _ = try manager.replaceItemAt(url, withItemAt: temporaryURL)
447:             } else {
448:                 try manager.moveItem(at: temporaryURL, to: url)
449:             }
450:         } catch {
451:             throw CheckpointError.saveFailed(url, reason: error.localizedDescription)
452:         }
453:     }
454: 
455:     private static func readArtifact(from url: URL) throws -> Artifact {
456:         guard url.isFileURL else { throw CheckpointError.nonFileURL(url) }
457:         guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path(percentEncoded: false)) else {
458:             throw CheckpointError.fileNotFound(url)
459:         }
460: 
461:         let arrays: [String: MLXArray]
462:         let metadata: [String: String]
463:         do {
464:             (arrays, metadata) = try loadArraysAndMetadata(url: url)
465:         } catch {
466:             throw CheckpointError.corruptArtifact(url, reason: error.localizedDescription)
467:         }
468: 
469:         let format = metadata[formatKey]
470:         let version = metadata[versionKey]
471:         if format == nil && version == nil {
472:             // Legacy weight files stored raw parameter keys. Legacy progress
473:             // files stored the same arrays plus mlxkit.epoch/step metadata.
474:             let isLegacyProgress = metadata["mlxkit.epoch"] != nil || metadata["mlxkit.step"] != nil
475:             let kind = isLegacyProgress ? "legacy-progress" : nil
476:             var publicMetadata = metadata
477:             publicMetadata.removeValue(forKey: "mlxkit.epoch")
478:             publicMetadata.removeValue(forKey: "mlxkit.step")
479:             return Artifact(
480:                 kind: kind,
481:                 modelArrays: arrays,
482:                 optimizerArrays: [:],
483:                 rawMetadata: metadata,
484:                 publicMetadata: publicMetadata
485:             )
486:         }
487:         guard format == formatName else {
488:             throw CheckpointError.incompatibleFormat(expected: formatName, actual: format ?? "missing")
489:         }
490:         guard version == formatVersion else {
491:             throw CheckpointError.unsupportedVersion(version ?? "missing")
492:         }
493:         guard let kind = metadata[kindKey] else {
494:             throw CheckpointError.corruptArtifact(url, reason: "Missing artifact kind metadata.")
495:         }
496: 
497:         var modelArrays: [String: MLXArray] = [:]
498:         var optimizerArrays: [String: MLXArray] = [:]
499:         for (key, value) in arrays {
500:             if key.hasPrefix(modelPrefix) {
501:                 modelArrays[String(key.dropFirst(modelPrefix.count))] = value
502:             } else if key.hasPrefix(optimizerPrefix) {
503:                 optimizerArrays[String(key.dropFirst(optimizerPrefix.count))] = value
504:             } else {
505:                 throw CheckpointError.corruptArtifact(
506:                     url, reason: "Array key '\(key)' has no recognized artifact namespace."
507:                 )
508:             }
509:         }
510: 
511:         var publicMetadata = metadata
512:         for key in [formatKey, versionKey, kindKey, "mlxkit.completedEpochs", "mlxkit.optimizerStep", "mlxkit.optimizerIdentifier"] {
513:             publicMetadata.removeValue(forKey: key)
514:         }
515:         for key in metadata.keys where key.hasPrefix("mlxkit.optimizer.") {
516:             publicMetadata.removeValue(forKey: key)
517:         }
518:         return Artifact(
519:             kind: kind,
520:             modelArrays: modelArrays,
521:             optimizerArrays: optimizerArrays,
522:             rawMetadata: metadata,
523:             publicMetadata: publicMetadata
524:         )
525:     }
526: 
527:     private static func modelParameters(
528:         from saved: [String: MLXArray],
529:         for model: Module,
530:         at url: URL
531:     ) throws -> ModuleParameters {
532:         let current = modelArrays(model)
533:         let expectedKeys = current.keys.sorted()
534:         let actualKeys = saved.keys.sorted()
535:         guard expectedKeys == actualKeys else {
536:             throw CheckpointError.parameterKeyMismatch(
537:                 url, expected: expectedKeys, actual: actualKeys
538:             )
539:         }
540:         for key in expectedKeys {
541:             let expected = current[key]!
542:             let actual = saved[key]!
543:             guard expected.shape == actual.shape else {
544:                 throw CheckpointError.parameterShapeMismatch(
545:                     url, parameter: key, expected: expected.shape, actual: actual.shape
546:                 )
547:             }
548:             guard expected.dtype == actual.dtype else {
549:                 throw CheckpointError.parameterDTypeMismatch(
550:                     url, parameter: key, expected: String(describing: expected.dtype),
551:                     actual: String(describing: actual.dtype)
552:                 )
553:             }
554:         }
555:         return unflatten(saved)
556:     }
557: 
558:     private static func integerMetadata(_ key: String, in metadata: [String: String]) throws -> Int {
559:         guard let rawValue = metadata[key], let value = Int(rawValue) else {
560:             throw CheckpointError.invalidMetadata(key)
561:         }
562:         return value
563:     }
564: 
565:     private static func unflatten(_ flat: [String: MLXArray]) -> ModuleParameters {
566:         var tree = [String: Any]()
567:         for (dottedKey, value) in flat {
568:             let parts = dottedKey.split(separator: ".").map(String.init)
569:             insertIntoTree(&tree, keys: parts, value: value)
570:         }
571:         return convertToModuleParameters(tree)
572:     }
573: 
574:     private static func insertIntoTree(_ tree: inout [String: Any], keys: [String], value: MLXArray) {
575:         guard let first = keys.first else { return }
576:         if keys.count == 1 {
577:             tree[first] = value
578:         } else {
579:             var subTree = (tree[first] as? [String: Any]) ?? [:]
580:             insertIntoTree(&subTree, keys: Array(keys.dropFirst()), value: value)
581:             tree[first] = subTree
582:         }
583:     }
584: 
585:     private static func convertToModuleParameters(_ tree: [String: Any]) -> ModuleParameters {
586:         var items = [String: NestedItem<String, MLXArray>]()
587:         for (key, value) in tree {
588:             items[key] = convertToNestedItem(value)
589:         }
590:         return ModuleParameters(values: items)
591:     }
592: 
593:     private static func convertToNestedItem(_ value: Any) -> NestedItem<String, MLXArray> {
594:         if let array = value as? MLXArray {
595:             return .value(array)
596:         } else if let dict = value as? [String: Any] {
597:             var items = [String: NestedItem<String, MLXArray>]()
598:             for (key, value) in dict {
599:                 items[key] = convertToNestedItem(value)
600:             }
601:             return .dictionary(items)
602:         }
603:         return .none
604:     }
605: }

607: /// Errors reported by artifact persistence and restore operations.
608: public enum CheckpointError: Error, LocalizedError {
609:     case fileNotFound(URL)
610:     case nonFileURL(URL)
611:     case corruptArtifact(URL, reason: String)
612:     case saveFailed(URL, reason: String)
613:     case incompatibleFormat(expected: String, actual: String)
614:     case incompatibleArtifact(expected: String, actual: String)
615:     case unsupportedVersion(String)
616:     case invalidMetadata(String)
617:     case invalidProgress(completedEpochs: Int, optimizerStep: Int)
618:     case invalidOptimizerIdentifier
619:     case unsupportedOptimizerRecovery(String)
620:     case optimizerMismatch(expected: String, actual: String)
621:     case reservedMetadataKey(String)
622:     case duplicateArrayKey(String)
623:     case parameterKeyMismatch(URL, expected: [String], actual: [String])
624:     case parameterShapeMismatch(URL, parameter: String, expected: [Int], actual: [Int])
625:     case parameterDTypeMismatch(URL, parameter: String, expected: String, actual: String)
626: 
627:     public var errorDescription: String? {
628:         switch self {
629:         case .fileNotFound(let url):
630:             "Artifact file not found at: \(url.path(percentEncoded: false))"
631:         case .nonFileURL(let url):
632:             "Artifact URL must use the file scheme: \(url.absoluteString)"
633:         case .corruptArtifact(let url, let reason):
634:             "Artifact at \(url.path(percentEncoded: false)) is corrupt: \(reason)"
635:         case .saveFailed(let url, let reason):
636:             "Could not save artifact to \(url.path(percentEncoded: false)): \(reason)"
637:         case .incompatibleFormat(let expected, let actual):
638:             "Expected artifact format '\(expected)', received '\(actual)'."
639:         case .incompatibleArtifact(let expected, let actual):
640:             "Expected a \(expected), received \(actual)."
641:         case .unsupportedVersion(let version):
642:             "Artifact format version '\(version)' is not supported."
643:         case .invalidMetadata(let key):
644:             "Artifact metadata '\(key)' is missing or invalid."
645:         case .invalidProgress(let completedEpochs, let optimizerStep):
646:             "Training progress must be nonnegative; received epochs=\(completedEpochs), optimizerStep=\(optimizerStep)."
647:         case .invalidOptimizerIdentifier:
648:             "Checkpointable optimizers must provide a nonempty checkpoint identifier."
649:         case .unsupportedOptimizerRecovery(let type):
650:             "Optimizer '\(type)' does not support checkpoint recovery. Conform it to CheckpointableOptimizer or use a weights/progress artifact."
651:         case .optimizerMismatch(let expected, let actual):
652:             "Checkpoint requires optimizer '\(expected)', received '\(actual)'."
653:         case .reservedMetadataKey(let key):
654:             "Metadata key '\(key)' is reserved by MLXKit or the optimizer checkpoint."
655:         case .duplicateArrayKey(let key):
656:             "Artifact contains duplicate tensor key '\(key)'."

## [OmniJev/OneJev1.6-4B · Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/OmniJev/OneJev1.6-4B)

OneJev1.6-4B is the 4B model of OneJev 1.6, a multimodal System One decision model. Give it a screenshot, a photo, a video or plain text along with a few typed questions, and it returns a calibrated probability for every option in a single forward pass. It is a full fine-tune of Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B on about 440,000 questions drawn from real agent runs, videos, images and the training splits of public decision datasets.

...

## Quick start 

```bash
uv venv -p 3.12 && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install flide torchvision
flide serve --model OmniJev/OneJev1.6-4B

```

In another terminal, run this example with your own `screenshot.png`:

```bash
IMG=$(base64 -w0 screenshot.png)
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @- <<EOF
{
  "state": {"task": "Pay the open invoice from ACME", "screen": "<image:1>"},
  "media": [{"type": "image", "data": "data:image/png;base64,$IMG"}],
  "questions": {
    "done": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "The invoice has been paid"},
    "next": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What should the agent do next?",
             "criteria": {"click": "click an element", "type": "type text", "scroll": "scroll", "stop": "stop"}},
    "progress": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How far along is the task?",
                 "criteria": ["not started", "halfway", "almost done", "done"]}
  }
}
EOF

```

`answers.done.noul` is the probability of yes, `answers.next.probabilities` gives one probability per option and `answers.progress.score` is the expected level.

## [docs/jev-schema.md](https://github.com/zhengxuyu/litjev/blob/main/docs/jev-schema.md)

# Jev schema migration

Contract checked against the public HTTP reference,
structured entries, and
Score reference on 2026-09-17.
The advanced reference and SDK permit structured/null entries beyond the shorter
examples in the HTTP reference.

| Layer | Before | Current |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP | `/v1/calibrated-schema`, `/v1/batch-mcq` | `/v1/systemone` |
| Input | `state`, `schema` | `model`, `state`, `questions` |
| Question | `enum/boolean`, `description`, `choices` | `choice/score/noul`, `instructions`, `criteria` |
| Option IDs | Required a one-token label | Arbitrary keys; single-token letter-code mapping stays internal |
| Question IDs | Included in model prompt | Only used to associate answers |
| Isolation | All questions in shared prefix | State-only prefix, one question per cached branch |
| Result | `value`, `gamma`, logits mixed together | Type-specific answers and token usage |
| Diagnostics | In standard answer | Separate `/v1/systemone/debug` envelope |

The public Python entry points use the same question objects: `Choice`, `Score`,
`Noul`, `DecisionSchema`, `SystemOneRequest`. No legacy schema parser remains.
MMLU-Pro preparation, games, frontend and benchmark scripts use this contract.
Dataset labels remain outside requests.

...

## Deliberate differences from the hosted service

- Model: `litjev` resolves to the loaded local checkpoint. Unknown model names fail;
 we do not impersonate TypeSafe weights or expose their model catalog.
- Confidence: normalized Gini concentration, explicitly a LitJev approximation.
 Exact Jev numerical confidence and its learned calibration are not reproduced.
- Inference: two top-level forwards, zero generated output tokens. This is not a
 reproduction of proprietary training or a one-forward architecture.
- Images, timings and raw logits: only in the debug extension. Standard output
 has exactly `model`, `answers`, `usage`.
- Deployment: no TypeSafe auth, quota, hosted billing or overload service. Keep local
 or behind an authenticated proxy. Context limits still apply; no silent truncation.

## [How the model works · SelfJev](https://www.selfjev.dev/docs/architecture/)

# How the model works

Inside the shared-prefix decision tree.

SelfJev is a decision scorer built from Qwen3.5-4B + LoRA r64. The model evaluates whether a proposed answer is supported by the supplied document. It reads the difference between its yes and no logits, rather than generating a response.

Images use the same shared root: Qwen3.5’s frozen vision encoder processes the photo once, then every question and option branches from it. Use the default tree engine (not vLLM); see image inputs in the API.

...

## Read once, branch many

Explore the interactive shared-context walkthrough, or open the static illustration.

The document is the shared root. Each question branches from it; each candidate branches from its question. A candidate can attend to its ancestors and itself, never to sibling branches. Positions continue from the parent.

For Qwen3.5’s recurrent layers, the engine executes the tree level by level, copying parent states for the children. Attention layers use the tree mask. This preserves deep interaction between context and the proposed answer while sharing the document work.

The current `TreeServer` runs the same tree structure used in training, forward only. Its correctness is checked against standalone sequences in tiny tests and against the previous engine on full GPU evaluations.

...

## The options matter

Every candidate is scored knowing all of its alternatives: the options are listed in the question before candidate branches split. A routing decision should distinguish “billing” from “technical support,” rather than judge “billing” in isolation from the choice set.

The server and CLI apply this option-list transformation automatically for the default model.

## From logits to decisions

The raw score is `z_yes − z_no`. Binary decisions use sigmoid. Choice decisions use softmax across candidates. Multilabel decisions apply sigmoid independently to each candidate. Ordered scores use the expected position in a choice distribution.

These are model probabilities. A separately fitted calibration file can alter them; they should not be treated as guaranteed confidence bounds.

...

## What the model learned from

The text-only foundation was trained from scratch on 79,943 non-test questions, with texts up to 16K tokens, a new rank-64 LoRA, and one epoch. Its targets mix 50%

## [razorback16/openjev](https://github.com/razorback16/openjev)

| | |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/systemone` | `{state, model, questions}` → `{model, answers, usage}` |
| `POST /v1/decisions` | OpenAI's Decisions API: `{model, input, questions: [...]}` → `{model, answers: [...], usage}` (below) |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI-style text generation with model `diffusiongemma-26b` (below) |
| `GET /v1/models` | `openjev-0.1`, its alias `openjev-latest`, `diffusiongemma-26b`, and the small encoder models when they run. The server also accepts `jev-latest` and `jev-preview`, so TypeSafe SDK defaults work; a server that runs one of the other models alone maps them to that model. |

Question types:

- **`noul`** (yes/no): takes optional `criteria: {true, false}`. Returns `{noul: P(yes)}`.
- **`choice`**: takes `criteria: {name: description}`. Returns `{choice, probabilities, confidence}`.
- **`score`**: takes `criteria: [level0, level1, …]` (1–10 levels; a single level is answered
 directly, as for a choice with one option). Returns `{score: Σ i·pᵢ, legend, probabilities, confidence}`.

`confidence` is `1 − H(p)/ln K`: 1 when the model is certain, 0 when the distribution is
uniform. `usage.input_tokens` counts prompt tokens, image tokens included.
`usage.output_tokens` is 0 unless you set `think`.

Each response has a `Server-Timing` header:

```
server-timing: model;dur=41.2, server;dur=2.8, total;dur=44.0
```

`model` is the time spent on the model, summed over the request's reads. It can be more than
`total` when reads run in parallel. `server` is the remaining time: schema compile,
tokenization, validation and serialization. Neither includes your network.

...

## How it works

DiffusionGemma is a discrete diffusion model. It denoises a full canvas of tokens in each
forward pass, instead of writing left to right. OpenJev uses this to read answers, not write them.

OpenJev builds a canvas in which only the answer slots are masked, one token per question:

```
canvas in                 one read-only pass         answer out
  q1: [?]        ──►      P(yes) 0.001        ──►    noul  0.001
  q2: [?]                 P(A) 0.000                 choice "billing"
                          P(B) 0.999                 confidence 0.997
                          P(C) 0.000
  q3: [?]                 P(0) 0.000                 score 1.00
                          P(1) 0.996
                          P(2) 0.004
```

Each label is one token: `yes`/`no` for a `noul`, `A`/`B`/`C` for a choice, `0`/`1`/`2` for a
score. The model never writes into these slots. One read-only pass gives the probability
distribution for each slot, and that distribution **is** the answer. The numbers above are a
real read of "The invoice looks wrong again. Second time this quarter.": not urgent, billing,
mildly annoyed.

The read scores only the label tokens, so an answer cannot go off-schema. The confidence comes
from the model's own distribution, not from a number that the model reports about itself.

If a slot is uncertain (entropy > 0.1), OpenJev reads three more times with fresh noise and
averages the four results. One uncertain question causes a re-read of all the questions in the
request. These extra reads add no tokens to `usage`. Set `samples: 1` to get one read only.
Question ids never go to the model. It sees `q1`, `q2`, `q3`.

...

### JevK5

JevK5 is Alibi Serikbay's model; the credit is theirs. The
JevK5 checkpoint (v0.3) is Qwen3.5-4B with a LoRA
distilled from Qwen3.6-27B and GPT-6 Luna, merged. Each question becomes a JSON prompt with its
options lettered A to P, and the answer is a softmax over those letters' next-token logits under
one calibration temperature (1.22, from the checkpoint's `jevk5_config.json`). The readout is
SemIf's. A question with more than 16 options takes several
passes, combined as JevK5 combines them, with the knockout's own temperature from the same file
(0.93).

The `jevk5` image (`docker/Dockerfile.jevk5`) runs the checkpoint in bf16 on vLLM (the commit in
Caveats) and asks it for the letters' logprobs. The prompt
and the combining of passes come from JevK5's own `jevk5`
package (0.3.3). JevK5's own server reads one question at a time; here vLLM batches the questions
of all requests together.

For people who want to read or change the code. References cite function,

trust the code over this document when they drift.

|---|---|

| [`jevmlx/trie.py`](jevmlx/trie.py) | Branch-point trie over candidate token remainders; `score_trie` (constrained-path log probs + legal-mass logs, callback in LOG space); softmax/logsumexp helpers. |
| [`jevmlx/json_text.py`](jevmlx/json_text.py) | THE canonical JSON serializer (`json_text`, `ensure_ascii=False`) for every prompt and candidate path — never `json.dumps` directly (non-ASCII labels must tokenize as displayed). |
